topic: Explain what a context switch preserves and the role of the scheduler in xv6 CPU multiplexing.
learner_profile: Undergraduate computer science student who has studied the supplied course material and introductory concepts; no unstated implementation-specific knowledge is assumed.

expected_evidence.quote: it saves the switched-from thread’s CPU registers, and restores the previously-saved registers of the switched-to thread
a kernel thread gives up the CPU by context-switching to that CPU’s “scheduler thread,”

review_criteria: Do not confuse a switch between kernel threads with saving an entire address space.
The explanation must identify saved/restored CPU registers and scheduling through the per-CPU scheduler.

topic: Analyze and justify a synchronization design when a kernel thread and an interrupt handler share a spinlock, including local and multiprocessor effects.
learner_profile: Undergraduate computer science student who has studied the supplied course material and introductory concepts; no unstated implementation-specific knowledge is assumed.

expected_evidence.quote: only sys_pause can release it, but sys_pause will not continue running until clockintr returns.
Interrupts may still occur on other CPUs, so an interrupt’s acquire can wait for a thread to release a spinlock; just not on the same CPU.

review_criteria: The scenario must state which CPU is interrupted and who owns the spinlock.
Reason through why the interrupted owner cannot release the lock while its same-CPU interrupt handler spins.
Disabling local interrupts does not replace mutual exclusion against other CPUs; preserve the role of atomic locks.
Difficulty requires linked reasoning about the deadlock and the limits of the proposed repair, not obscure terminology.

topic: Evaluate a producer-consumer wait protocol for lost wakeups and condition rechecking using the supplied xv6 sleep_prepare/sleep/wakeup interface.
learner_profile: Undergraduate computer science student who has studied the supplied course material and introductory concepts; no unstated implementation-specific knowledge is assumed.

expected_evidence.quote: sleep_prepare(chan) must be called either before checking the condition, or before releasing the lock that protects the condition.
For this reason sleeping always occurs inside a loop that re-checks the condition

review_criteria: Use the frozen sleep_prepare/sleep interface rather than silently substituting an older xv6 API.
Give enough scheduling and lock details for every candidate protocol to be evaluated.

Reject explanations that hold the condition lock while sleeping and thereby prevent the producer from making progress.

topic: Recognize transaction atomicity and the effect of COMMIT versus ROLLBACK in a simple PostgreSQL transfer.

expected_evidence.quote: A transaction is said to be atomic: from the point of view of other transactions, it either happens completely or not at all.
we can issue the command ROLLBACK instead of COMMIT, and all our updates so far will be canceled.

review_criteria: State the transaction boundary and whether COMMIT or ROLLBACK is reached.
Exactly one answer must preserve the all-or-nothing treatment of the transfer.
Do not present atomicity as a guarantee that every business rule or every concurrent invariant is automatically enforced.

topic: Trace what ordinary SELECT statements may observe under PostgreSQL Read Committed in a two-session schedule.
learner_profile: Undergraduate computer science student who has studied the supplied course material and introductory concepts; no unstated implementation-specific knowledge is assumed.

expected_evidence.quote: a SELECT query (without a FOR UPDATE/SHARE clause) sees only data committed before the query began
two successive SELECT commands can see different data, even though they are within a single transaction

review_criteria: Supply initial values, each statement start, relevant commit times, and all modifications.
Use ordinary non-locking SELECT and explicitly identify the isolation level.
Each read must be evaluated against its statement snapshot while allowing the transaction to see its own earlier writes.
Do not incorrectly infer one fixed snapshot for the whole Read Committed transaction.

expected_evidence.quote: a query in a repeatable read transaction sees a snapshot as of the start of the first non-transaction-control statement

Do not substitute BEGIN time for the first snapshot-taking statement.

topic: Evaluate an application retry design after a PostgreSQL serialization failure when reads determine later writes.
learner_profile: Undergraduate computer science student who has studied the supplied course material and introductory concepts; no unstated implementation-specific knowledge is assumed.

expected_evidence.quote: retry the complete transaction, including all logic that decides which SQL to issue and/or which values to use.
Transaction retry does not guarantee that the retried transaction will complete; multiple retries may be needed.

review_criteria: Specify transaction boundaries and the read-dependent application decision; do not rely on hidden external side effects.
Exactly one option must correctly rerun both reads/decisions and writes rather than only the failed statement.

Do not conflate all persistent constraint errors with retryable serialization failures.

topic: Compare receiver flow control and network congestion control, then justify the active sending constraint in contrasting TCP situations.
learner_profile: Undergraduate computer science student who has studied the supplied course material and introductory concepts; no unstated implementation-specific knowledge is assumed.

expected_evidence.quote: Flow control involves preventing senders from over-running the capacity of receivers.
the maximum number of bytes of unacknowledged data allowed is now the minimum of the congestion window and the advertised window.

review_criteria: Separate receiver buffer pressure from congestion along the network path.
If numeric windows are used, provide their units and outstanding unacknowledged data; distinguish total allowed in-flight bytes from additional send allowance.
A justified comparison must identify which constraint is active in each case and why changing the other limit alone may not help.
Do not infer that a large advertised receive window proves the path is uncongested.
